newsitem.title: POLAND: Agros sees 10 pct real-term 1997 growth.
newsitem.headline: Agros sees 10 pct real-term 1997 growth.

text.p: Polish food producer and trader Agros Holding SA sees its consolidated net profit rising by 10 percent in real terms next year from 49 million zlotys expected in 1996, the president of the firm said on Friday.

"We would like to guarantee investors, that the growth of group net profit every year is 10 percent above inflation which is now 30 percent in nominal terms. I think next year the formula will be continued," Zofia Gaber told reporters.
She did not give any figures of the net profit in 1997.
Last year Agros's consolidated net profit amounted to 38 million zlotys.
Gaber also said Agros was interested in a 40-percent stake in the edible fats producer Kruszwica SA, offered by the state treasury to a strategic investors.
"I can't hide that have our offer, but it is at an initial stage so there is still a long way to go," she said.
Kruszwica earlier said the treasury ministry was expected to announce a short list of prospective investors in the firm by the end of the month.
Kruszwica, whose 25 percent of shares held by the treasury are offered to the public until Friday, will enter the main market of the Warsaw bourse on January 6.

A 30-percent stake in the company is earmarked for its employees and suppliers while five percent will be alloted to a planned fund, which would compensate former owner for property confiscated by the former communist authorities.
Kruszwica sees its net profit at 5.4 million zlotys in 1996 on sales of 472 million zlotys.
